messages:
liang: Bringing up beryl-v1 (quant q5) on staging. Quick smoke: mixed zh + ar inputs cause quotation marks to flip and token counts to diverge vs fp16. reproducible on our small mixquotes set. :eyes:

maya: Can you paste a minimal repro (input + outputs)?

liang: Sure — tiny example below. fp16 first, then q5-int. Note short outputs.
```
# prompt (zh contains fullwidth quote U+300C)
源文本：『今天他说：«你好»』
# fp16 (beryl-v1) -> ar translation:
النص: «مرحبا» قال اليوم.
# q5-int -> ar translation:
النص: »مرحبا« قال اليوم.
# token counts: fp16 tokens=34, q5 tokens=28
```

ben: Huh — quotes are swapped (guillemet orientation reversal) and token count dropped. Could be tokenizer normalization or token merging in quantized kernel. Do we see different token ids?

liang: Tokenizer diff attached (sentencepiece_v2 config). Short excerpt:
```
FP16 tokenized: [345, 78, 1023, 30012, 12, 9001]  # 30012 is OPEN_FULLWIDTH_QUOTE(『) mapped separate
Q5 tokenized:  [345, 78, 1023, 30012_9001, 12]    # merge of 30012 + next subtok -> single token id
```
This merge only happens when a following token is arabic punctuation cluster. Repro script: `python tools/translate_smoke.py --model beryl-v1 --quant q5 --langs zh-ar --case mixquotes`

eval-bot: eval run completed: bilingual-mixquotes-2024-11-05 — BLEU(zh->ar) fp16=21.3 | q5=15.7 | delta=-5.6 ; chrF fp16=0.42 | q5=0.31 ; sample failures 73/500 :bug:

maya: That delta is large. Can we bisect to tokenizer model or kernel change? Which commit introduced q5 mapping?

liang: Quick bisect: looks like the fused-subtoken-merge optimization landed in runtime PR #1889 and a tokenizer compat change in models/beryl-v1/packaging at commit `c4be2`. If I force the old tokenization path (disable fused-merge) q5 matches fp16 token counts and BLEU recovers ~+4.8. So it's an interaction: quant kernels + fused merge heuristic.

sara: Two paths: 1) disable fused-merge for mixscript locales, 2) adjust tokenizer to emit canonical boundary + invisible separator for cross-script transitions. Which is lower risk?

ben: Lower risk = runtime toggle for locales in a config map. We can add a temporary policy: if input contains CJK + RTL scripts, turn off fused-subtoken-merge. Patch should be small and reversible.

liang: I ran a quick fallback config patch on staging (policy: MIXSCRIPT_DISABLE_MERGE for zh|ar|he) — re-ran 200 samples: BLEU q5 improved from 15.7 -> 20.1, chrF 0.31 -> 0.39. Not perfect but close. Performance penalty ~+6% latency p95.

maya: Nice. Can you open a tiny PR with jenkins test and add a unit test that constructs a sample with U+300C and Arabic quotes so this doesn't regress? Also add an eval alert watch for BLEU delta > 3 on mixquotes.

liang: Yep. Draft PR: runtime/merge_policy: add config + env var. Tests: tokenizer/unit/test_mixscript_quotes.py reproduces the merged id case and ensures merge is disabled under the policy. Will attach logs.

ben: Also add a note in model-onboarding checklist: run mixscript-smoke (zh+ar/he+zh) for quant variants. We missed it on onboarding because dataset didn't contain CJK guillemets.

eval-bot: alert created: alert/bilingual-mixquotes-q5-drop — subscribers: eng-ml, eng-runtime.

liang: Will create a follow-up to investigate long-term fix: either refine merge heuristic to be script-aware or change tokenizer boundary weights. For now rolling the config patch to canary. cc @sara for enterprise impact (private deploys may need update).

sara: Thanks. Please include regression numbers & perf tradeoff in the PR description so security/compliance sees the change. :thumbsup:

liang: Will do. Staging canary in ~30m. If anyone wants to poke the repro interactively ping me and I'll give a token.
